Hearers matched the sound to tones of about 33-80 Hz and compared it to an idling diesel engine. The team found no signal matching it. Source: Los Angeles Times (1993), Mullins & Poteet, JASA (1994).

A 2026 PLOS One study of 28 hum hearers found most had normal low-frequency hearing and no low-frequency ear emissions, and suggests tinnitus for many cases, not all. Back in 1993 the Taos team's ear expert had ruled tinnitus out. Source: PLOS One, LA Times.
